title: Bharata: Governing in Rama's Name
subtitle: The sandals become a sign of delegated rule

learningObjectives.text: What does Bharata assign the work of government to?
How long does Bharata vow to wait for Rama?

sandals.author: Valmiki
sandals.locator: Ayodhyakandam · Section CXII; Ayodhyakandam · Section CXII, normalized characters 3098-3503
sandals.excerpt: Thereupon taking off his sandals, that highly energetic one gave them to the magnanimous Bharata. Bharata, bowing down unto the sandals, said, "O hero, for four and ten years shall I, wearing matted locks and bark, and subsisting upon fruits and roots, O scion of the Raghu race, expecting thy arrival, remain outside the city, having, O subduer of foes, made over the task of government unto thy sandals.
sandals.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

narrativeBlocks.title: Bharata refuses to replace Rama
narrativeBlocks.body: In Dutt's Ayodhyakandam, Bharata returns to Rama and asks him to take the throne. Rama's sandals become part of their agreement about who will govern.

narrativeBlocks.title: A symbol of delegated rule
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Dutt's English rendering; whitespace normalized): “Thereupon taking off his sandals, that highly energetic one gave them to the magnanimous Bharata. Bharata, bowing down unto the sandals, said, "O hero, for four and ten years shall I, wearing matted locks and bark, and subsisting upon fruits and roots, O scion of the Raghu race, expecting thy arrival, remain outside the city, having, O subduer of foes, made over the task of government unto thy sandals.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A vow with a time limit
narrativeBlocks.body: Bharata says he will remain outside the city in ascetic dress for fourteen years and assign the work of government to the sandals while awaiting Rama's return.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep this within Volume 1
narrativeBlocks.body: Dutt's first volume contains the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam. This episode is a literary account of a specific succession, not evidence that sandals universally signify kingship in Indian practice.

narrativeBlocks.title: Authority is represented in absence
narrativeBlocks.body: The passage shows Bharata acting as steward while treating Rama as the rightful ruler in this version.
